transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Suncrest Head of AI), Liam (Platform), Ravi (Security), Sofia (PM)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll focus on the POC scope — workload modeling, benchmarks, and success criteria.
[00:18] Maya: Hi — we want to validate a customer support NLP pipeline, mainly real-time answer generation and a reranking step. Primary asks: latency below SLOs, understand cost at scale, and prove security controls.
[00:34] Diego: Great. Can you give us current traffic signals — QPS, concurrency, avg tokens?
[00:42] Liam: Sure, it's rough but peak QPS is around 200-300 depending on campaign days, sustained ~60 QPS; concurrencies at the front end ~40-50. Typical user message is short, 12-25 input tokens, output avg 40-80 tokens. Some outliers up to 400 tokens for long histories.
[01:05] Sofia: We also have a reranker that takes top-10 candidates and runs a lightweight scoring model, that adds additional calls — about 0.3x of the gen QPS.
[01:18] Diego: Ok so effective gen QPS plus rerank load is ~250QPS at peak, with burstiness. For POC we should model spiky traffic and baseline sustained.
[01:30] Maya: Success criteria — practical list: (1) 95th pct latency for single-turn responses under 300-350ms; (2) total cost per 1k requests under our budget target — we'll share; (3) evidence of KMS-integrated key management and audit logs; (4) ability to run in our VPC/private deployment eventually.
[01:55] Ava: Helpful. We'll propose both Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated runbooks. Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower per-token cost, but increases setup.
[02:08] Ravi: For security, we need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration, customer-managed KMS, and retention policy controls. Can you confirm the private deployment options?
[02:20] Ava: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem variants, integrates with KMS/HSM for key control, and we can provide audit logs. We'll attach the security pack.
[02:31] Liam: Back to traffic modeling — what do you need from us to simulate accurately?
[02:37] Diego: The most helpful is request/response logs showing timestamps, token counts, and response times — anonymized. If not available, a histogram of input/output tokens and per-minute QPS will suffice. We'll build a harness that replays traces with jitter and concurrency.
[02:55] Maya: We'll pull a 2-week rolling sample and scrub PII.
[03:02] Ava: Timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — agree on scope and data; week 1 — setup benchmark harness and run synthetic baseline; week 2 — run full benchmark including cache and batching variants; week 3 — analyze results and iterate; week 4 — final results + decision. So a 4-week POC.
[03:25] Sofia: That matches our internal timeline.

[03:35] -- Technical dive (Diego leads) --
[03:40] Diego: On modeling: we care about QPS, concurrency, latency SLOs, and token distribution. We'll target scenarios: baseline (sustained 60 QPS), burst (250 QPS for 3-5min), and heavy outlier (single long request up to 400 tokens). We'll also test cold-start behaviours for KV cache misses.
[04:05] Maya: How do you handle prefix caching, KV cache, and reranker batching?
[04:12] Diego: Redwood runtime supports prefix caching and KV cache to avoid re-computing earlier tokens; continuous batching improves throughput but increases tail latency. For conversational context, KV cache helps a lot if repeated prefixes exist across users. Reranker we can run as separate dedicated pool or via same model with smaller batch sizing.
[04:33] Liam: Any recommended concurrency target per GPU?
[04:36] Diego: It varies by model, quantization, and GPU type. For many open LLMs, we see optimal GPU utilization at 8-24 concurrent streams for short seqs. We'll provide modeled concurrency suggestions after we see token distributions.
[04:50] Maya: We plan to use a 7B-ish model variant for initial tests, maybe quantized; down the road we may try 13B.
[04:57] Diego: Good—smaller models are cheaper and hit lower latencies. Quantization like 4-bit helps a lot. We'll include those variants in the benchmark.

[05:10] -- Benchmark specifics and metrics --
[05:12] Diego: Metrics we'll measure: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tail latency during bursts, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k responses, and failure rate. We'll capture token breakdowns (input vs output) to guide batching and rate limiting.
[05:30] Ava: Please include cost delta between hosted and dedicated at the target QPS. We want per-user cost guidance.
[05:36] Diego: Will do. Also testing batching thresholds — e.g., batch windows 5ms, 10ms, 25ms — to show latency vs throughput tradeoffs.

[05:48] Ravi: For security we need network architecture diagram for Private deployment and list of access controls — RBAC, SSO, audit log retention. Also how KMS is integrated and whether keys can be customer-managed.
[06:01] Ava: We'll attach Redwood security deck and a one-page private deployment sketch. Keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM integration.

[06:10] -- Modeling details (QPS/concurrency calculation example) --
[06:15] Diego: Quick calc: if peak gen QPS = 250 and avg tokens out = 60, that's 15k tokens/sec outbound. With an avg token latency budget of 300ms, we need enough GPU capacity to handle concurrent token streams; batching can raise throughput but may push 95th pct higher. For a 4-week pilot we'll show configs that meet 95th < 350ms.
[06:43] Maya: Can you simulate the reranker overhead?
[06:46] Diego: Yes — we model reranker as a follow-up request pattern: 0.3x additional calls with smaller tokens (avg 12). We'll run end-to-end synthetic flows to measure combined latency and costs.

[06:58] -- Notes about imperfect transcripts & name swaps --
[07:02] Sofia: small note: transcripts sometimes say 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'Redwood dedicate' in notes, ignore typos.

[07:10] -- Questions from Suncrest on SLAs & rollouts --
[07:15] Maya: For canary and rollout policies, how does Redwood support A/B or traffic split?
[07:20] Ava: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, auto-fallback, and routing by policy (latency/cost/region). We'll demo the console in the follow-up.

[07:30] -- Pricing and cost modeling conversation --
[07:33] Ava: We'll provide a cost spreadsheet showing hosted per-token rates and Dedicated reserved capacity pricing. Expect Dedicated to lower per-token cost at sustained loads but requires commitment.
[07:45] Liam: Any quick ballpark? At sustained 200 QPS we expect significant savings on Dedicated, what numbers should we assume?
[07:52] Diego: Ballpark only — Dedicated could be 30-50% lower per-token at sustained high QPS, depends on model/quantization. We'll provide precise estimates in the POC plan.

[08:05] -- Operational concerns --
[08:08] Ravi: What about observability? We need per-route token & cost breakdowns, tracing, and alerting hooks.
[08:15] Ava: Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-model dashboards, traces, and error analysis. We'll include retention options as add-ons.

[08:25] -- Timeline recap and acceptances --
[08:28] Ava: Recap: Suncrest to share logs and security constraints by 5/11. Redwood to share POC plan and pricing by 5/10 and run baseline harness by 5/14. Week 2 target benchmark run with both hosted and dedicated configs. Final analysis week 3-4.
[08:45] Maya: Sounds good. One ask — please include a sample run for both short-turn (12 in / 40 out) and long-turn (120 in / 300 out) to see tail behavior.
[08:55] Diego: We'll include those.

[09:00] -- Closing --
[09:03] Ava: Thanks all, we'll send the plan and security docs. Any final Qs?
[09:07] Ravi: No, thanks — looking forward to the network walkthrough.
[09:10] Maya: Thanks everyone.

[09:15] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had a few mis-attributions and some product names mangled (e.g., 'Redwood dedicate' / 'KV cash' instead of KV cache). We kept informal interjections and filler words to preserve realism.
